title: Xiong, Z., Lin, Y., Xie, W., He, P., Liu, Z., Tang, J., Lakkaraju, H., & Xiang, Z. (2025). How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior.
senal_calidad: Table 1/2 (p.4/6) and Fig.3/4 (experience-following, error propagation) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a core empirical memory-management study, squarely on-topic.

title: Xu (2025). Memory Management and Contextual Consistency for Long-Running Low-Code Agents.
senal_calidad: RECONSIDERAR: Appendix A's own simulation code (hardcoded exponential-decay and hand-clamped ranges explicitly commented 'for realistic visualization') indicates Figure 2, and plausibly Table 1, are synthetic illustrations rather than measured agent runs; reference [6] also appears to attribute the real experience-following/self-degradation study (cf. the Xiong et al. paper in this same digestion wave) to different, seemingly fictitious authors and a mismatched venue (Nature Communications). Digested per protocol; flagging for human review given the evidence-fabrication risk.

title: Jayanti and Han (2026). Enhancing Model Context Protocol (MCP) with Context-Aware Server Collaboration.
senal_calidad: Table 2 (TravelPlanner) and Table 3 (REALM-Bench) anchor the numbers; small-scale paper (anonymous GitHub repo, only 2 benchmark tasks, authors explicitly note no hardware/parallelism controls in Limitations) -- RECONSIDERAR generalizability.

title: Anderson (2026). The AI Codebase Maturity Model: From Assisted Coding to Fully Autonomous Systems.
senal_calidad: Table 1-2 (level/feedback-loop inventory) and the Case A/B examples anchor the numbers; single-practitioner, self-authored experience report (IBM Research, written with Claude Code assistance per its own disclosure), not peer-reviewed -- RECONSIDERAR given the n=1, self-reported nature of the evidence.

title: Wang and Li (2023). Learning from Mistakes via Cooperative Study Assistant for Large Language Models.
senal_calidad: Table 2 (p.6, main results) + the 'failure can sometimes be more valuable than success' discussion (p.6, §4.4). Clearly on-topic negative-knowledge memory paper; not RECONSIDERAR.

title: Yang et al. (2023). Failures Pave the Way: Enhancing Large Language Models through Tuning-free Rule Accumulation.
senal_calidad: Table 1 (p.5, BBQ-Lite) + Table 4 (p.6, ablation) + Fig.3/4 (mistake-rate reduction, out-of-domain transfer) are load-bearing. Not RECONSIDERAR — a foundational negative-knowledge/rule-accumulation paper, squarely on-topic.

title: Zheng, S., He, K., Yang, L. y Xiong, J. (2024). MemoryRepository for AI NPC.
senal_calidad: Table 3 (p.11, MemGPT comparison) + §VI.B.1 (retrieval-degradation trade-off) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a direct long-term/human-like memory architecture paper for LLM agents.

title: Behrouz, A., Zhong, P. y Mirrokni, V. (2024). Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time.
senal_calidad: Ancla: Tabla 1 (p.13, perplejidad/accuracy) y Tabla 2 (p.13-14, NIAH); es arquitectura de memoria EN PESOS entrenables, no un sistema de memoria externa tipo agente — RECONSIDERAR aplicabilidad directa al harness MF (LLM congelado + docs).

title: Wang et al. (2025). Unveiling Privacy Risks in LLM Agent Memory.
senal_calidad: Ancla: Table 1 (main attack results + ablations) + Table 2/Figures 2-3 (configuration sweep: scoring function, memory size, retrieval depth) + Table 3 (backbone comparison). Directly on-topic memory-security paper (arXiv 2502.13172); no RECONSIDERAR needed, the security angle is a first-class MF concern (FIDELIDAD).

title: Ge, Y., Romeo, S., Cai, J., Shu, R., Benajiba, Y., Sunkara, M., & Zhang, Y. (2025). TReMu: Towards Neuro-Symbolic Temporal Reasoning for LLM-Agents with Memory in Multi-Session Dialogues.
senal_calidad: Table 5 (p.9, GPT-4o results + ablation) and §4.2 discussion (memory hurts sufficiently-large-context models but helps GPT-3.5) are the load-bearing findings. Not RECONSIDERAR — a direct memory + temporal-reasoning paper for multi-session dialogue agents.

title: Masoor (2025). SAMEP: A Secure Agent Memory Exchange Protocol for Persistent Context Sharing in Multi-Agent AI Systems.
senal_calidad: RECONSIDERAR: section 5.2 explicitly discloses the headline Table 1 results ('73% reduction', p<0.001, etc.) are 'projected performance results based on averaged benchmarks from distributed systems literature', i.e. NOT measured from a running SAMEP implementation -- attaching p-values to a non-experiment is a red flag; frozen extraction correctly scored evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA only (no ABLATION/BENCHMARK-E2E), consistent with this being unvalidated. Single-author independent-researcher preprint (arXiv 2507.10562), no peer review found. Treat any 'finding' from this paper as architecture-proposal-only, not empirical evidence.

title: Ouyang et al. (2025). ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory.
senal_calidad: Table 1 (p.7, WebArena) + Table 2 (SWE-Bench-Verified) + the AWM-degrades-on-Multi-subset finding (§4.2) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a leading reasoning-memory paper, squarely on-topic and highly relevant to MF's negative-knowledge/consolidation axes.

title: Chen et al. (2026). HaluMem: Evaluating Hallucinations in Memory Systems of Agents.
senal_calidad: Table 3 (p.11, per-stage hallucination results) + Table 5 (write-time bottleneck) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a rigorous operation-level hallucination benchmark directly on MF's FIDELIDAD axis, evaluating today's real production memory systems (Mem0, MemOS, Zep, etc.).

title: Tablan et al. (2025). Smarter Together: Creating Agentic Communities of Practice through Shared Experiential Learning.
senal_calidad: Fig.1 (code quality by backbone) and Section 4.4-4.5 (helpfulness bands, 98.2% figure) anchor the numbers; industry paper (The Memory Company / Moonsong Labs) evaluated only with SYNTHETIC experiential traces from one LLM (Section 4.1) rather than real multi-agent/multi-user community usage -- RECONSIDERAR how far the 'shared community' claim is validated versus a single-epoch synthetic proxy.

title: Wei et al. (2025). A-MemGuard: A Proactive Defense Framework for LLM-Based Agent Memory.
senal_calidad: Ancla: Table 1 (direct-poisoning ASR across 4 backbone/retrieval configs) + Table 2 + Figure 3 (indirect self-reinforcing-error-cycle ASR over interaction rounds) + section 5 multi-agent scalability result (0.950 task success). Rigorous, well-controlled security paper (arXiv 2510.02373); clearly on-topic, no RECONSIDERAR needed.

title: Lindenbauer et al. (2025). From Knowledge to Noise: CTIM-Rover and the Pitfalls of Episodic Memory in Software Engineering Agents.
senal_calidad: Table 1 (p.4, 6-configuration ablation) + §5.1 qualitative causal-tracing case studies (p.4-5, the 'clean' and 'GRANDMA LIKES PASTA' cases) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a rigorous, well-isolated negative-result paper on episodic memory for SE agents, high-value for MF's NEGATIVO/anti-poisoning stance.

title: Joshi, T., Chowdhury, S. y Uysal, F. (2025). SWE-Bench-CL: Continual Learning for Coding Agents.
senal_calidad: RECONSIDERAR: los experimentos principales de aprendizaje continuo (memory-enabled vs disabled comparando LLMs) estan formulados como hipotesis 'ongoing' (Sec.8); los unicos numeros duros vienen del experimento preliminar de incompatibilidad de harness (Sec.5) y de poisoning (Sec.4.2).

title: Zeppieri (2025). MMAG: Mixed Memory-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models Applications.
senal_calidad: Evidencia CUALITATIVA (estudio de caso Heero, Sec 6), sin ablation ni benchmark publico; plan_estado=SI segun input aunque el paper no discute planificacion explicita — RECONSIDERAR si el facet plan_estado esta bien asignado.

title: Alqithami, S. (2025). Forgetful but Faithful: A Cognitive Memory Architecture and Benchmark for Privacy-Aware Generative Agents.
senal_calidad: RECONSIDERAR -- STRONG evidentiary flag: the abstract's headline number (Hybrid composite approximately 0.911, 'best composite performance') directly CONTRADICTS the paper's own Table 2 (Hybrid measured at 0.589+/-0.009, ranked LAST of 5 reported policies; Random Drop tops at 0.635). No occurrence of 0.911 elsewhere in the body substantiates it. Also: the Reflection-Summary policy (1 of the 6 named in the abstract) is entirely ABSENT from Table 2's main ranking (footnote: 'will be inserted once its aggregates are finalized') -- an incomplete-results preprint (arXiv 2512.12856, Dec 2025, single author). Treat this paper's headline claims with caution; the architecture (MaRS typed/provenance memory) is sound and citable, the composite-score claims are not.

title: Duong (2025). PBFT-Backed Semantic Voting for Multi-Agent Memory Pruning.
senal_calidad: RECONSIDERAR -- SEVERE integrity flag: section V.C ('Results and Analysis') contains verbatim leaked LLM-assistant commentary referring to 'the user's original draft' and hedges like 'assuming this refers to...', explicitly states 'For this draft, a textual summary is provided' INSTEAD of tables/figures, and the paper admits NO ablation study was run. This strongly suggests the evaluation section was drafted/rationalized by an LLM from the abstract's claimed numbers rather than reporting a real executed experiment. Single-author preprint (arXiv 2506.17338). Recommend human review before citing any numeric claim from this paper; the PBFT+semantic-voting+decay ARCHITECTURE (section III, deterministic algorithms) is a legitimate design contribution independent of the evaluation's credibility.
